title: ER-DCIM: Error-Resilient Digital CIM Architecture with Run-Time MAC-Cell Error Correction
problem: Digital compute-in-memory (DCIM) macros are susceptible to SRAM cell errors under low-voltage operation (needed for high energy efficiency), but traditional SRAM error correcting codes (ECC) that correct errors in a single read-out row are incompatible with DCIM's simultaneous multi-row readout for MAC computation, leaving MAC-cell errors uncorrected.
motivation: Low-voltage operation is essential for maximizing DCIM energy efficiency, but voltage scaling increases SRAM cell error rates; uncorrected MAC errors accumulate and substantially degrade neural network inference accuracy, making reliable low-voltage DCIM operation unsolved.
method: ER-DCIM introduces three mechanisms: (1) a residue code-based MAC error correction scheme that detects and corrects additive errors in the MAC accumulation result in real time during DCIM computation — the first such mechanism for DCIM; (2) a progressive cell error correction mechanism that identifies and corrects underlying SRAM cell errors incrementally without stalling computation; (3) a mode switcher that repurposes redundant error-resilient logic (reserved for low-voltage protection) to boost performance in high-voltage mode, avoiding area waste.
key_novelty: Residue code-based real-time MAC error correction for digital CIM, the first mechanism to correct additive errors in DCIM MAC results during live computation rather than at the SRAM cell or row level.
contributions: Residue code-based real-time MAC-level error correction for DCIM, the first of its kind.
Progressive cell error correction avoiding computation stalls during SRAM repair.
Mode switcher that reconfigures error-resilient logic for throughput improvement in high-voltage mode.
ER-DCIM maintains high throughput and energy efficiency without accuracy loss in both low-voltage and high-voltage operating modes.

metrics.other: Maintains accuracy without loss in both low-voltage and high-voltage modes; no accuracy degradation stated vs. baseline

baselines: Standard digital CIM without error correction
limitations: Residue code overhead and the cost of progressive cell error correction in terms of area and timing closure are not quantified in the abstract.
primary_theme: Run-time MAC-level error correction for reliable low-voltage digital compute-in-memory
